title: Array Methods
summary: map, filter, reduce, find, some, every and flatMap: LINQ for JavaScript.

steps.title: Arrays and the LINQ you already know
body: Arrays grow and shrink like `List<T>`: `push`, `pop`, `length`, `includes`, `indexOf`. The methods below take a callback and return **new arrays**, just like LINQ (but they run immediately: there is no deferred execution).
The callback also receives the index: `xs.map((x, i) => ...)`.

steps.explain: `filter` keeps the odd numbers, `map` multiplies them. Node prints arrays as `[ 10, 30, 50 ]`. The original array is untouched.

steps.prompt: Match each method to its LINQ equivalent.

steps.title: reduce
body: `reduce` walks the array carrying an **accumulator**. Always pass the starting value:
const cart = [{ price: 300, qty: 2 }, { price: 150, qty: 1 }];
const total = cart.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.price * item.qty, 0);   // 750
It can build any shape, such as a count per key:
If a plain `map`/`filter` says it, prefer those: they read better.

steps.explain: `find` returns the first match, or `undefined` when nothing matches. `?.` protects the property read.

steps.title: Order summary
prompt: Each order is `{ customer: string; lines: { sku: string; qty: number }[] }`. Write:
1. `totalQty(orders)`: the total quantity across all lines of all orders (use `flatMap` and `reduce`).
2. `skus(orders)`: every distinct sku, in the order first seen.
{ customer: "a", lines: [{ sku: "tea", qty: 2 }, { sku: "cake", qty: 1 }] },
starter: type Order = { customer: string; lines: { sku: string; qty: number }[] };
solution: type Order = { customer: string; lines: { sku: string; qty: number }[] };
return orders.flatMap(o => o.lines).reduce((sum, l) => sum + l.qty, 0);
template: { customer: "a", lines: [{ sku: "tea", qty: 2 }, { sku: "cake", qty: 1 }] },
hints: `orders.flatMap(o => o.lines)` gives one flat array of lines.
For distinct values: keep an element only when `indexOf` finds it at its own index (or use a `Set`, next lesson).
